answer: Assign each account a living trellis planted with a distinct kernel seed variety, staked beside a marked karst rock in a shared community garden. Weekly, the account photographs its trellis with the karst marker and a dated newspaper, showing vine growth and the seed packet's unique code. Two neighboring gardeners countersign the growth stage. A Sybil farm would need a separate real trellis, a distinct seed variety, and months of visible growth per fake identity, so bulk identities become slow, costly, and easy to spot when growth stages do not match the season.
